title: Readiness 2 · Classes through lookups
prompt: TaskItem is supplied. Its Owner may be null. Write two methods. public static TaskItem Renamed(TaskItem task, string title) returns a copy with the new title and the same Id and Owner. public static Dictionary<string, int> CountByOwner(List<TaskItem> tasks) returns the number of tasks for each owner. Tasks whose Owner is null are counted under the key "Unassigned". An empty string is a real owner name and gets its own key.
hints: Which owner values are there to tell apart: a name, an empty string, and what else?
Turn a null owner into the key "Unassigned" before you touch the dictionary. Leave an empty string as it is.
Use task with { Title = title } for the copy. For the counts, use task.Owner ?? "Unassigned" as the key and add 1, starting a new key at 1.
checks: Practice.Renamed(new TaskItem(2, "Ship", null), "Send") == new TaskItem(2, "Send", null)
checkLabels: Renamed must change the title and keep the Id and Owner.
Renamed must keep a missing Owner missing.
The 2 tasks with no owner must be counted under "Unassigned".
An empty owner name is its own key, with 1 task.
The board must give exactly three keys.
An empty list must give an empty dictionary.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Treats an empty owner name as a missing owner.
Uses a missing owner directly as a dictionary key.

feedback: Look at how a null owner, an empty owner name and a real name are each turned into a key. They must give three different keys.
